summary: The antler Chief, grass mantle, bare-chested Scout and travelling herder establish a promising Stone Age lineup. However, several garments still read as modern shorts or matching shirt-and-trouser sets. Preserve the strong role silhouettes while correcting garment construction, prop clearance and small-scale detail.
problems: The Gatherer's straight, separately enclosed thigh pieces read unmistakably as modern shorts, especially on the blue variant. The grass collar does not overcome that underlying clothing read.
The Hearthkeeper resembles a coloured tracksuit with a decorative fur collar. Default sleeves remain enabled, and the long, parallel leg pieces have trouser-like hems.
The Flintworker's smooth diagonal bodice and regular lower tabs need stronger hide construction; the small rectangular tool head reads more like a generic hammer than chipped stone.

The Hearthkeeper and Chief's rounded shoulder pieces read as strings of cream-coloured blobs rather than folded hides. The Chief remains recognisable, but the crowded pale chest ornaments weaken the material read.
The Scout's spear and herder's staff share the arm centreline through much of the upper limb, creating intersection risks. The herder's inward-turning crook also overlaps the hood silhouette.

Several identity details are too small to carry at stream scale: belt stones, basket strips, shell beads and face markings. The herder's hood and luggage communicate travel better than the tiny shell decoration communicates a distinct visiting culture.
fix:
Flintworker of the Sinew Seam: Keep the one-shoulder silhouette and tied hair. Replace the regular lower tabs with three unequal, overlapping hide flaps and give the diagonal wrap one broad folded edge with a few chunky sinew stitches. Make the tool head an asymmetric faceted stone wedge, approximately 25% larger, visibly lashed to its handle.

Overlapping-Grass Gatherer: Remove the shorts-shaped thigh boxes. Build a short, uneven grass-and-hide wrap with overlapping front/back panels and separate leg-bound side flaps; do not bridge both moving legs with one rigid block. Preserve the broad green mantle, but stagger its strip lengths. Simplify the basket to a strong bowl, rim and thick handle visibly held by the hand.

Hearthkeeper in the Folded Shoulder Hide: Add sleeves to the hide list and replace the narrow custom sleeve boxes with short, irregular hide shoulder coverings. Rebuild the lower garment as an overlapping, split hide apron with unequal leg-bound side panels rather than two trouser tubes. Replace the shoulder spheres with broad faceted folds, leaving one prominent fastening and a clear pale shoulder silhouette.

Young Ridge Scout: Preserve the exposed torso, narrow pelt and feather. Move the spear shaft outward from the arm centreline to a visible hand grip, then angle it away from the shoulder. Use a chipped, asymmetric stone point with a substantial binding; retain the compact loincloth rather than adding shorts.

Chief of the Great Branched Antlers: Keep the antler crown and raised staff as the primary office symbols. Replace the round fur clusters with a broad, angular shoulder pelt; simplify the chest decoration to three large teeth on a visible cord. Give the lower hide an irregular overlapping hem. Shape the staff's ivory block into a recognisable bone or animal-head emblem with one large dark recess.

Far-Roving Shell-Cowl Mammoth Herder: Keep the enclosing hood, patchwork hide and bedroll. Replace the bead row with three larger shell clusters repeated on the hood and pack, making the visiting culture readable from above. Move the staff outside the arm and turn its hook outward so it clears the hood. Make the paired tusk ornaments visibly attached to a hide yoke. Check every kit in walking poses at the actual 40-degree gameplay camera and final stream size.
